detail:
twining-conservative-utf8/1.0.0, table proven-utf8-bytes/1, provenance "proven-upper-bound", envelope_overhead_tokens 8, every class ratio 1.0.

Why 1.0: in a byte-level BPE whose vocabulary holds all 256 single bytes, every token decodes to at least one byte, so tokens(s) <= utf8_byte_length(s). That is a proof, needs no model or network, and cannot undercount. It is also about 4x loose on English prose, which is a real cost: a 4000-token budget now genuinely guarantees <= 4000 tokens, but buys roughly a quarter of the prose it used to.

The machinery to tighten it with EVIDENCE is in place and unused: buildCalibrationTable() takes per-class observed maxima, multiplies by a safety factor, and CLAMPS to the proven bound (a measurement may only ever tighten, never loosen). scripts/calibrate-tokenizer.mjs measures against the Anthropic count-tokens API over test/fixtures/tokenizer-corpus/ and refuses to emit a table without a key. It is never run from tests.

DECISION FOR THE LEAD: ship the proven bound as-is (safe, loose), or run one calibration pass with a key and ship a measured table. The corpus is 5 documents - enough to exercise the harness, not enough to bound production text. I did not fabricate ratios to close the gap.

DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED while building: at a small budget the packet's own framing (incomplete banner + omission manifest) exceeded the budget, so the bound was violated exactly when it mattered. C26 section 6's second accepted terminal shape (refused_incomplete) is now the fallback, with budget_infeasible:true when even the refusal cannot fit — an honest overflow rather than an invisible one.
summary: DP4 tokenizer ships a PROVEN bound (1 token/UTF-8 byte, ~4x loose) not a calibrated one — no API key here, and inventing ratios is the fabrication the bound exists to prevent
